# A reclaim-route arm pins the same live pane after the transit

## Context

Item 4 of #18621, split into its own leaf so the arm can ship while item 2 (the reconcile of a returning item) is still an investigation — the same split item 3 received as #18632. Two witnesses of #18621 read a torn-out pane as lost after Reset and after Undo; the isolation ([receipt](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18621#issuecomment-5647537174)) showed the document moves some 30 ms after the click and the live pane embodies some 330–360 ms later, and every "no pane follows" read sat inside that window. #18632 / PR #18635 then made a never-connected vessel's lease end retain the pane instead of destroying it, and deferred the re-tree half of its AC-1 to this arm. Neither behaviour has a committed regression arm on the flagship: the only receipts are scratch rigs and hand runs.

## The Problem

The reclaim route (Reset, Undo, `Show … here`) moves a live pane across a window boundary in two steps that are hundreds of milliseconds apart: the document commit, then the component's embodiment in the destination window. A test that reads once after the document settles cannot tell a lost pane from one in transit, and a test that reads the document cannot see a pane that never embodies. The regression that matters is not "the document says home" but "the SAME live instance is mounted where the document says, with its `windowId` flipped and its tab in the home strip" — asserted after the transit, on the instance, never on the document alone.

## The Architectural Reality

- `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs`: the topology bar's `Reset to default` button (`createTopologyBar`) calls `resetTopology()`, which reclaims shipped panes into main in one Group write while retaining every participant; `Undo` / `Redo` are the Group's (`TransactionManager.undo({groupId})`). `WorkspaceController#syncTopologyBar` adds `Open <key> as window` / `Show <key> here` per popup state; `mountTopologyWorkspace` mounts a retained participant inline into the root.
- `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs#resolveProjectedPane` falls through to the consumer's cached `resolvePane` on the reclaim route, so the pane comes home as the same instance; `Neo.container.Base#add` sets `windowId` and forces `mounted = false` across a window boundary, which is why embodiment trails the document.
- `Neo.manager.Transaction#reconnectLeaseMs` (default 20000) bounds a released or never-bound slot; at lease end the Workstation's retained headless vessel keeps its pane parked (`mounted: false`, not destroyed) since #18635. `getPaneIdentity(itemId)` returns the live instance id — a rebuilt pane carries a new id, so identity equality is the "no `createPane`" observable.
- Tier: `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/*NL.spec.mjs` with the `neuralLink` fixture (`WorkstationTopologyGroupsNL.spec.mjs` is the pop-out precedent, `WorkstationNL.spec.mjs`'s Group-undo arm the same-pane precedent). These specs need `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT`; without it `playwright.config.e2e.mjs` deselects them (`testIgnore`), and `buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs` keeps every workstation spec outside the CI e2e-engine tier (GPU). This is an L3 local / matrix arm, not a CI check.

## The Fix

One spec, `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationReclaimEmbodimentNL.spec.mjs`, two arms on the real Workstation:

1. **Reset and Undo** — pop `feed` out through the focus-gated pop-out header action into a real vessel window; press the real `Reset to default`; poll until the SAME pane (`getPaneIdentity` before and after) is embodied in the root — `windowId` = root, mounted, in the root DOM, gone from the vessel DOM, its tab present in the home strip; press the real `Undo`; poll until the same instance is embodied in the vessel again.
2. **Lease end and re-tree** — shorten `reconnectLeaseMs` through the live manager, pop out and close the vessel at its `popup` event (never connected); poll until the slot leaves the manager; assert the pane is parked, not destroyed, and still the same identity; click `Show <vessel> here`; poll until the same instance is embodied in the root.

Both arms read embodiment from the component through the Neural Link and poll the transit; neither asserts the document alone.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 — Arm 1 passes on the real Workstation: after Reset the same live pane instance is embodied in the root (`windowId` flip, mounted, root DOM, home-strip tab, vessel DOM empty) and after Undo it is embodied in the vessel again; the identity read through `getPaneIdentity` is unchanged across both.
- [ ] AC-2 — Arm 2 passes: a vessel closed at its popup event keeps its pane parked (`mounted: false`, not destroyed) past the lease end, the manager drops the slot, and `Show … here` re-trees the same instance into the root without a new id.
- [ ] AC-3 — Two positive controls recorded in the PR: with #18635's engine change reverted, arm 2 is red on "parked, not destroyed"; with the Workstation rebuilding a pane on every resolution, arm 1 is red at its first identity-bearing read.
- [ ] AC-4 — The PR body states the tier honestly: the spec is Brain-dependent and outside the CI e2e-engine selection, so the evidence is the local L3 run with the runtime root, and no CI coverage is claimed.

## Out of Scope

- #18621 item 2 (the reconcile of a returning item whose live pane sits in another window) and its cockpit witness.
- The lease-end retention itself (#18632, shipped in PR #18635) and the Group history semantics of Undo / Redo.
- Native (pointer / titlebar) vessel conversion, and the App Worker console assertion (#18554).
- Returning workstation specs to the CI e2e-engine tier.

## Avoided Traps

| Rejected | Why |
|---|---|
| A single read after the click | The document moves some 30 ms after the click, the pane some 330–360 ms; a read between them is indistinguishable from a lost pane. Poll the transit. |
| Asserting the document | The document was right 300 ms before a user could see anything; the regression is embodiment. |
| A tab-chrome homecoming witness alone | A reparented pane arrives naked through `add`; the strip tab is asserted beside embodiment, never instead of it. |
| `isDestroyed === false` on a live pane | The engine only writes `isDestroyed` on destroy, so a live instance reads `undefined` through the Neural Link. Normalise to `=== true`. |
| Reading the holders once at the popup event | The tear-out commits asynchronously to the `popup` event, and commits whether or not the vessel connects. Poll. |
| Claiming CI coverage | Workstation specs are GPU-excluded from the CI tier and the fixture is Brain-dependent. |
